definition: Appropriating habits, observances, or practices as self-sufficient or identity-supporting; the habit-and-observance member of the fourfold upādāna framework.
notes: The project now keeps taking habits and observances personally as the default because it aligns the compound with the upādāna headword, whose compound context rule directs the four members of the family to carry the headword’s appropriative force. The issue is not wholesome discipline itself, but appropriative fixation on forms and procedures, which the appropriation reading makes explicit. Clinging to habits and observances remains the familiar comparative alternate and is still acceptable in source-facing or continuity-sensitive prose, including where continuity with the corresponding fetter entry sīlabbata-parāmāsa matters. This term belongs to the four clinging types and should be read alongside sīlabbata-parāmāsa. The OSF glossary supports this by treating sīlabbatupādāna as a specific appropriation mode rather than as discipline itself.

context_rules.notes: Use this as a controlled alternate when continuity matters more than maximizing explicit alignment with the headword, including alongside the fetter entry sīlabbata-parāmāsa.

context_rules.notes: Use when the repo's broader upādāna logic should remain audible.

context_rules.notes: Allow this as a compact controlled alternate only when brevity is needed. Do not rotate it back into the house default.

example_phrases.notes: Shows one member of the fourfold set.

version_notes: Harmonised with the upādāna headword and the rest of the fourfold family: the default moves from clinging to rules and observances to taking habits and observances personally. The clinging rendering is retained as the continuity alternate, and the sīlabbata stem now renders as habits and observances across every record that carries it.

authority_basis.scope: Named in notes as support for the current sīlabbatupādāna policy.

translation_policy.default_scope: Use 'taking habits and observances personally' as the default rendering in the fourfold upādāna framework unless a recorded context rule overrides it.
translation_policy.when_not_to_apply: Use 'clinging to habits and observances' only when continuity-sensitive prose or source-facing expectations make it the clearer choice. Do not reduce the term to discipline.
translation_policy.drift_risk: Prevents drift back toward 'discipline', and keeps the compound aligned with the upādāna family rather than with plain rule-language.
